name: CueMem

paper.title: CueMem: Cue-Guided Context Reconstruction for Long-Term Conversational Memory

construction.unit: dialogue turn, reached via (subject, relation, object) triple cues
construction.kept_as: verbatim turns + extracted triple cues pointing to source turn
construction.processing: LLM extracts zero or more triples per turn; cues embedded; turn-graph edges

organization.stores: cue records, source-turn nodes, graph edges
organization.index: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 cue embeddings; temporal-window and cue-kNN semantic edges

management.operations: ADD cues per new turn; no UPDATE; DELETE via standard policies (proposed)
management.conflicts: none stored; answer prompt prioritises most recent evidence
management.forgetting: time-decay or LRU deletion suggested, not evaluated

retrieval.candidates: top-m cues by cosine similarity, mapped to source-turn anchors
retrieval.selection: anchors plus one-hop temporal/semantic neighbours, chronological order
retrieval.budget: about 2K tokens of reconstructed context; m, w, k values not retrievable

use.context: reconstructed original turns in chronological order
use.reasoning: single answer call with recency-priority instruction

stages.ingestion: The dialogue history is treated as a chronological sequence of turns (user utterance + agent response, with timestamps).
stages.construction: An LLM extracts zero or more (subject, relation, object) triples per turn as memory cues, each with a pointer to its source turn; cues are embedded (all-MiniLM-L6-v2).
stages.organization: A turn-level graph with temporal edges (turns within a window w) and semantic edges (top-k cue-embedding neighbours mapped back to their source turns).
stages.update: ADD inserts cues and turn nodes for new turns; no specialised UPDATE (newer facts are added as new cues and the answer prompt says to prioritise recent evidence); DELETE can use standard forgetting policies such as time decay or LRU.
stages.retrieval: The query is embedded, top-m cues retrieved, their source turns used as anchors, and anchors plus their one-hop temporal/semantic neighbours are collected and ordered chronologically (about 2K tokens).
stages.answer: The reconstructed original-turn context is given to the LLM with an instruction to prioritise the most recent information closest to the question time.

summary: Uses extracted triples only as retrieval cues that point back to source turns, then reconstructs verbatim dialogue context by expanding over a temporal/semantic turn graph.
